verdicts.summary: The status waiter cannot block past 5s. Fiber.join is only an observer of the forked fetch, so a queued or hung fetch does not hold the caller. Failures that land after the waiter returns still gate the next poll via retryAt.
evidence: .repos/effect-smol/packages/effect/src/internal/effect.ts:839-846 (fiberJoin observes only, does not interrupt target)
apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:474-506 (poll under KeyedLock, bounded by the 5s waiter)
verdicts.consequence: None for the status path. The poll returns after at most 5s, using the last fetched refs.
verdicts.scenario: Four stalled fetches saturate statusFetchProcesses, then a fifth status poll for a queued repo. The waiter times out at 1315 and returns None. The queued fiber keeps running and is not interrupted. Also tried: a fetch fails after the waiter returned. tapError at 1300 records retryAt, and the next poll returns early at 1280 until it passes. Both paths are consistent.

verdicts.summary: The unbounded Fiber.await at line 2670 runs while the pull still holds the per-repo KeyedLock remote write lock. A stalled background fetch therefore blocks every remote-status refresh for that cwd for the fetch's full lifetime, not just the pull's 30s.
evidence: apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1258-1292 (fetch timeout 5min, forceKill 1s, forked and queued behind 4 permits)
apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:481-492 (refreshRemoteStatus holds withRemoteWriteLock and calls maybeAutoPull inside it)
apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:514-523 (refreshStatus takes same lock and calls maybeAutoPull)
packages/shared/src/KeyedLock.ts:47-53 (blocking semaphore per key, no try-lock)
verdicts.consequence: A user clicking Refresh status, or the turn-end PR refresh (RunFinalizationService.ts:111 calls refreshPullRequestStatus under the same lock), waits in the KeyedLock queue until the stalled fetch finishes or times out. That is up to about 5 min plus 2s, or more if the fetch was queued. Before the commit the pull did not wait on the fetch, so this lock hold was about 30s at most.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Repo R is on its default branch, clean, with autoPull on. Local remote-tracking refs are already behind HEAD, for example after an earlier auto-pull failed on a ref lock. 2) The poll runs refreshRemoteStatus under the R lock. Its status fetch F starts and the remote hangs. The waiter returns at 5s (1314). 3) remote.behindCount>0 from stale refs, so maybeAutoPull calls pullCurrentBranch. 4) It reaches Fiber.await(F) at 2670 and blocks with the R lock held. 5) A user's vcsRefreshStatus RPC for R waits at VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:514 until F ends.

verdicts.summary: forceKillAfterMs passes unchanged to the spawner. The number is read as milliseconds, and undefined takes the old one-second path for every other caller.
verdicts.consequence: None. Other execute callers keep undefined, so they keep the one-second grace and no SIGKILL. The status fetch gets a 1s SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL window.
verdicts.scenario: Tried: a non-status caller with forceKillAfterMs undefined. ChildProcess.make receives forceKillAfter undefined, and the spawner takes the isUndefined branch. Tried: the number 1000 reaching Duration.toMillis, which is identity for a number.

verdicts.summary: Retry guard depends on `symbolic-ref --short HEAD` equalling `refName`. If Git abbreviates the branch name because of an ambiguous ref, the lock retry is silently skipped and the pull fails. Low: the failure is loud and nothing is lost.
evidence: apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2642-2643 (refName comes from status porcelain branch.head, which is not abbreviated)
verdicts.consequence: The pull reports the lock error and the retry against the upstream never runs, so the recovery path is lost for that repo.
verdicts.scenario: The repo has branch main and also a tag named main. `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` returns `heads/main` when Git considers `main` ambiguous. That behaviour is Git's, not in this checkout, so this scenario depends on it. Then currentBranch !== refName, the retry is skipped, and the user sees the lock error.
verdicts.missing: Git's --short disambiguation rules are outside the checkout.

verdicts.summary: Manual pull (vcsPull) is not under the remote write lock, so a status fetch that starts after pullCurrentBranch's pending check is not awaited. The lock retry also does not wait, so the same ref-lock failure can recur.
evidence: apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2241-2252 (statusDetails can start a fetch via refreshStatusUpstreamIfStale)
apps/server/src/ws.ts:2757-2763 (vcsPull calls gitWorkflow.pullCurrentBranch with no remote write lock)
verdicts.consequence: The pull can fail with 'could not update a local reference' even though the fix was meant to recover from ref-lock collisions. The window is small because the lock is held briefly during ref update.
verdicts.scenario: Manual pull starts with no pending fetch. A statusDetails call on the same repo starts a fetch after the 2667 check, once the 15s cache has expired. Its ref update collides with the pull's fetch. The retry at 2722 runs without waiting and can collide again.

verdicts.summary: The dedupe check-then-set on statusFetches is not atomic. The runtime can yield between Map.get at line 1283 and Map.set at line 1310, so two concurrent callers can both start a fetch for one key. The first fiber's onExit can then delete the second's entry.
evidence: apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1281-1311 (get, yield* forkIn, then set, all inside Effect.uninterruptible)
apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1303-1307 (onExit deletes by key, not by identity)
verdicts.consequence: Two concurrent git fetch processes for one remote. One may fail on a ref lock and start a 30s cooldown. The pull's check at 2667 can miss the second fiber and run without waiting.
verdicts.scenario: Two status calls for the same repo and remote arrive together. Call A does get, then the runtime yields after its op budget before set. Call B does get, sees nothing, and forks. A then sets its fiber, overwriting B's entry. If B exits first, its onExit deletes A's entry. Probability is low because the window is a few ops.
